text:
clara: Heads-up: compliance scanner flagged several archived DB snapshots in glacier-prefix with no ServerSideEncryption metadata at 06:18 UTC. Likely re-encrypt/transfer issue.

sec-bot: ALERT: SNAPSHOT_NO_SSE - s3://redwood-glacier/prod-db-snaps/2026-05-04 - 9 objects. alert id SEC-20260504-08

dan: Which pipeline wrote those objects? Vendor-sync or our internal archiver?

clara: Looks like vendor-sync-run-7 performed a multipart copy/compose step around 06:15. CloudTrail shows PutObjectCopy without ServerSideEncryption; the vendor role "arn:aws:sts::999999:assumed-role/vendor-sync-role" executed the copy.

evan: I pulled the copy command from the job logs: the tool uses S3 multipart compose and explicitly sets metadata-directive=REPLACE but doesn't pass --sse. So it effectively stripped encryption metadata.

yuki: Oof. Why does vendor role have write/modify to that prefix? I thought vendor-sync was scoped to read-only.

dan: Recent RBAC change (PR #5402) granted vendor-sync-role s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectAcl for the archive prefix to support multipart writes. It rolled last week.

sec-bot: change-note: RBAC change added on 2026-05-01T21:05 by infra:team.

clara: Immediate mitigation: 1) pause vendor-sync jobs, 2) re-copy affected objects with --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/aa11bb22, 3) add an S3 bucket policy to reject PutObjectCopy/PutObject with metadata-directive=REPLACE unless request includes x-amz-server-side-encryption header, 4) revert RBAC if necessary.

evan: Re-copy started for 9 objects; we're rate-limiting to avoid KMS throttles. Took a sample head-object before copy to confirm ServerSideEncryption absent.

yuki: Long-term: vendor roles must not be able to replace metadata on encrypted buckets. We should push an IAM deny statement on the archive prefix: deny s3:PutObjectCopy when encryption header missing. Also add PR gate: any RBAC granting PutObject to external roles flagged for security review.

dan: Agreed. I'll open a hotfix PR to tighten role scope and add terraform guardrails to prevent granting PutObject on encrypted buckets without kms:Encrypt permissions and an automated policy lint.

audit-bot: ACTION: Logged incident INC-20260504-08. Required artifacts: CloudTrail copy events, RBAC diff PR #5402, vendor sync job logs, list of affected objects.

clara: We also need to confirm whether any GETs occurred on those objects while unencrypted. Check S3 access logs + CloudTrail for s3:GetObject on those keys 06:15-06:25.

evan: querying logs now. No external GETs found; only internal retry logs from the vendor sync process and our re-copy process.

yuki: Good. For remediation, we'll: 1) enforce bucket policy to reject metadata-replace without SSE, 2) revoke vendor-sync write permissions until RBAC tightened, 3) add CI lint for terraform to block granting write permissions to external principals on encrypted buckets, 4) add a Splunk alert for head-object responses missing ServerSideEncryption on archive prefixes.

dan: I'll own RBAC revert and terraform guards. clara, evan: you own the re-copy and verification. yuki: please draft the compliance message; we need to be transparent but accurate: no external access detected, re-encrypted, RBAC tightened.

sec-bot: Vendor sync jobs paused. Re-copy completed for 9 objects at 06:28 UTC. KMS usage within limits.

clara: Thanks. We'll follow-up with a short postmortem (owners assigned) and a retrospective to avoid granting metadata-replace capabilities to third parties.

(ends)
